items.title: H.P.C. Religion
items.decryption: H (Harsha: Shaiva to Buddhist), P (Pallavas: Jain to Shaiva), C (Chalukyas: Vedic to Puranic/Shaiva).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming Harshavardhana was a Buddhist from birth; he was originally a Shaiva.
Confusing the Pallava king Mahendravarman I's conversion (Jain to Shaiva) with others.
Thinking the Chalukyas were exclusively Shaiva; they were great patrons of Jainism and Vaishnavism too.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Core Centers

  • Kannauj (Harsha)
  • Kanchi (Pallavas)
  • Badami/Aihole (Chalukyas)

Key Figures

  • Hiuen Tsang (Witness)
  • Appar (Shaiva Saint)
  • Ravikirti (Jain Poet)

Religious Dynamics

  • Harshavardhana: Transition from Surya/Shiva worship to Mahayana Buddhism, climaxing in the Prayag Assembly.
  • Pallavas: Shift from Jainism (Mahendravarman) to Nayanar-led Shaivism. Rock-cut temples as propaganda.
  • Chalukyas: Vedic sacrificial culture combined with Puranic temple construction; religious pluralism (Jainism flourished at Aihole).
